question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.
To bring to light
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To disclose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To bring to light" means to reveal or make known something that was hidden or secret, i.e. to disclose it. (किसी छिपी हुई बात को उजागर करना)
◦ Example: The investigation brought to light several irregularities in the company's accounts.

• The image behind the idiom is of bringing something out of darkness into the light so that it becomes visible to everyone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To engage in conversation means to start talking with someone; it has nothing to do with revealing hidden facts.

• Option 2: To lighten means to make something less heavy or less serious, or to brighten something — an unrelated meaning.

• Option 4: To disengage means to release or free oneself from an engagement or connection, which is unrelated to revealing information.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of revealing/hiding: "To let the cat out of the bag" (to reveal a secret unintentionally), "To come to light" (to become known), and "To throw light on" (to explain or clarify something).

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(a) false news websites
(b) spreading propaganda about politics
(c) thrive because the advertisements and politicians
(d) and social networking sites
(e) make a lot of money
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. adcbe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arranging the parts in the order a-d-c-b-e gives the meaningful sentence: "False news websites and social networking sites thrive because the advertisements and politicians spreading propaganda about politics make a lot of money."

• Rule: In sentence-rearrangement questions, first identify the subject group (here, "(a) false news websites" joined with "(d) and social networking sites"), then the verb phrase that follows the subject ("(c) thrive because the advertisements and politicians"), and finally the part that completes the reason/cause ("(b) spreading propaganda about politics" followed by "(e) make a lot of money", since it is the advertisements and politicians who make money by spreading propaganda).

• Checking grammatical agreement: the compound subject "websites... and... sites" takes the plural verb "thrive", and the later subject "advertisements and politicians" correctly takes the plural verb "make".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (aecbd) is incorrect because it places "(e) make a lot of money" immediately after "(a) false news websites", breaking the logical subject-verb link and producing a meaningless sequence.

• Option 3 (adecb) is incorrect because "(e) make a lot of money" is placed before "(c) thrive because...", so the sentence loses its main verb "thrive" in the correct position and becomes incoherent.

• Option 4 (aedcb) is incorrect for the same reason — "(e)" interrupts the subject group "(a)...(d)", so the sentence no longer reads meaningfully.

NOTE

• In para/sentence-jumble questions, always locate the independent subject-verb pair first — it usually anchors the correct order — and then attach modifying or reason clauses around it.

• Watch for connector words like "because", "and", "who", "which" — they usually signal which part must immediately follow another.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
P) willing to go
Q) is not
R) my son
S) camping
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. RQPS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arranging the parts in the order R-Q-P-S gives the meaningful sentence: "My son is not willing to go camping."

• Rule: The subject must come first ("R) my son"), followed by the verb "is not" (Q), then the complement "willing to go" (P), and finally the activity "camping" (S) that completes the infinitive "to go camping".

• This follows the basic English sentence structure: Subject + Verb + Complement/Object.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (SPRQ) is incorrect because it begins with "camping", which cannot logically start the sentence and leaves no proper subject-verb opening.

• Option 3 (PQRS) is incorrect because it places "willing to go" before the subject "is not... my son", producing an ungrammatical, meaningless order.

• Option 4 (QRSP) is incorrect because the verb "is not" is placed before the subject "my son", and "camping" appears before "willing to go", breaking both word order and meaning.

NOTE

• In such jumbles, always look for the subject phrase (a noun/pronoun like "my son") — it almost always opens a simple declarative sentence.

• Verb phrases such as "is not", "was", "has been" typically follow the subject directly.

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
The ointment will help to _____ the wound.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. heal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "heal" means to cure or make a wound/injury better, which fits the context of an ointment helping the wound to recover.

• Rule — Homophones: Homophones are words that sound alike but have different spellings and meanings. Here, "heel", "heal", and to a lesser extent "he'll" sound similar, so the correct one must be chosen based on meaning.

• In the given sentence, only "heal" (verb, to cure) makes sense with "the wound"; the ointment helps the wound heal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "he'll" is the contraction of "he will", a pronoun + auxiliary verb, which does not fit grammatically before "the wound".

• Option 2: "heel" refers to the back part of the foot, unrelated to curing a wound.

• Option 4: "kneel" means to go down on one's knees, which is unrelated to healing a wound.

NOTE

• Commonly confused homophones for SSC exams: heel/heal/he'll, there/their/they're, allowed/aloud, weather/whether, stationary/stationery, principal/principle.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Attack
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Defence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Attack" means to make a violent offensive move against someone/something (हमला करना), so its opposite is "Defence", which means to protect or guard against an attack (रक्षा करना).

• Rule: Antonym questions require identifying a word that expresses the opposite core meaning, not merely a related or associated word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Ambush (घात लगाना): A surprise attack from a hidden position — this is actually a synonym-type word for attack, not its opposite.

• Option 3: Production (उत्पादन): Means the act of making or manufacturing something; unrelated to the idea of attack or defence.

• Option 4: Engagement (व्यस्तता/मुठभेड़): Can mean an appointment, involvement, or a military encounter, but it is not the direct opposite of "attack".

NOTE

• Other common antonym pairs tested in SSC exams: Offence × Defence, Aggressive × Passive, Assault × Protect, Invade × Retreat.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. It was as simple as announcing what you have in your store or the services you offer in your premises.
B. Over the years, advertising has evolved into a major industry that goes beyond informing to persuading and influencing.
C. Advertising was initially meant to make people aware of the goods available in the market.
D. It is a form of brainwashing consumers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. CABD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arranging the sentences as C-A-B-D gives a logically coherent paragraph: C introduces the original purpose of advertising, A elaborates on that original simplicity, B shows how advertising evolved over time, and D gives the concluding critical remark.

• Rule — Paragraph coherence: The first sentence of a jumbled paragraph is usually the one that introduces the topic in general terms (here, "C: Advertising was initially meant to make people aware..."), followed by sentences that elaborate (A), then show development/contrast (B, signalled by "Over the years"), and finally a concluding statement (D).

• The linking phrase "Over the years" in sentence B clearly marks a transition from the past (introduced in C and A) to a later stage, so B must come after A, and the closing judgement D must come last.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BADC) is incorrect because it starts with "Over the years", which needs a prior reference point (the initial purpose of advertising) that has not yet been introduced.

• Option 2 (ADBC) is incorrect because it places the idea of evolution (B) before the original purpose (C), disturbing the chronological flow.

• Option 3 (DABC) is incorrect because it opens with the concluding critical statement D, which should logically come at the end, not the beginning.

NOTE

• In paragraph-jumble questions, look for a sentence that introduces the topic without using pronouns like "it", "this", or "they" referring back to something unstated — such a sentence is usually the opening line.

• Transition words like "over the years", "however", "therefore", "as a result" are strong clues to sequence, since they connect to something already stated.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
We should plan our actions judiciously before going to war.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Irrational.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Judiciously" means in a wise, sensible, and well-judged manner (विवेकपूर्ण ढंग से), so its opposite is "Irrational", meaning not guided by reason or sound judgement (अतार्किक).

• Rule: For antonym questions on adverbs, first find the antonym of the root adjective (judicious → irrational/unwise) and then match it with the closest option in form and meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Irreverent (अनादरपूर्ण): Means showing a lack of respect; it is about disrespect, not about poor judgement.

• Option 3: Irrelevant (अप्रासंगिक): Means not connected to the matter at hand; it does not mean "unwise".

• Option 4: Irritatingly (चिड़चिड़ाहट से): Relates to causing annoyance, which is unrelated to the sense of judgement in "judiciously".

NOTE

• Judicious is related to "judge" and "judgement" — remember the family: judicious (wise), judicial (relating to courts of law), judgmental (quick to criticize).

• Other antonym pairs with the "ir-" prefix often tested: Regular × Irregular, Responsible × Irresponsible, Relevant × Irrelevant.

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: It is said that Joseph was not ready to go to war.
option_2: Karl Marx was a renowned social scientist.
option_3: Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity.
option_4: It is impossible to wake Christine up in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity" is grammatically incorrect because the singular collective noun "force" is followed by the plural verb "are", causing a subject-verb agreement error.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement with collective nouns: A collective noun (like force, army, team, committee) normally takes a singular verb when it is treated as a single unit. The sentence should read either "Indian force is known..." or, if referring to multiple forces, "Indian forces are known...".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "It is said that Joseph was not ready to go to war." is grammatically correct — the impersonal construction "It is said that..." followed by the past tense "was" is properly formed.

• Option 2: "Karl Marx was a renowned social scientist." is grammatically correct — the singular subject "Karl Marx" correctly takes the singular past-tense verb "was".

• Option 4: "It is impossible to wake Christine up in the morning." is grammatically correct — the phrasal verb "wake... up" and the infinitive construction "It is impossible to..." are both properly used.

NOTE

• Collective nouns commonly tested for singular/plural agreement: team, family, army, jury, government, committee, audience, crowd.

• If a collective noun's individual members are emphasised as acting separately, a plural verb may be used (e.g. "The committee are divided in their opinions"), but the default rule tested in SSC exams is singular agreement.

question:
Select the correct meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Rina pulled a long face since her husband had not bought her a diamond necklace on their anniversary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To look saddened.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to pull a long face" means to look unhappy, disappointed, or sad, usually by visibly showing a gloomy expression. (उदास चेहरा बनाना)
◦ Example: He pulled a long face when he learnt that his leave had been cancelled.

• The image behind the idiom is of a face that appears to droop or lengthen with sadness or disappointment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To be euphoric (अत्यंत प्रसन्न होना): Means to feel intense happiness or elation — the opposite of the intended meaning.

• Option 2: To be ecstatic (आनंदमग्न होना): Means to feel overwhelming joy or excitement — again the opposite of sadness.

• Option 4: To be electrified (रोमांचित होना): Means to be suddenly filled with great excitement or energy, unrelated to sadness.

NOTE

• Other idioms of sadness/displeasure often asked in SSC: "To be down in the dumps" (to feel very sad), "To be in the doldrums" (to be in low spirits), and "To cry over spilt milk" (to lament something that cannot be undone).

question:
Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank.
The thought of eating half-cooked food under compulsion fills me with _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. repugnance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "repugnance" — a strong feeling of dislike or disgust towards something.
◦ Example: She looked at the rotten food with repugnance.

• Spelling key: RE + PUGN + ANCE. Note the sequence "u" before "g" in "pugn", and the ending "-ance", not "-ence". The word comes from the Latin word repugnare, meaning "to fight against".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "ripugnance" — incorrect; the first vowel should be "e", not "i".

• Option 2: "repegnance" — incorrect; the middle vowel should be "u" (pugn), not "e" (pegn).

• Option 4: "repugnence" — incorrect; the ending should be "-ance", not "-ence".

NOTE

• Related word: repugnant (adjective, meaning distasteful or offensive).

• Other commonly confused "-ance/-ence" endings in SSC spelling questions: performance, maintenance, existence, occurrence, persistence.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.
The resturant offers a wide variety of dishes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. resturant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The incorrectly spelt word is "resturant"; the correct spelling is "restaurant" — a place where meals are served to customers for payment.

• Spelling key: REST + AU + RANT. Note the "au" after "rest", which is often missed. The word comes from the French word restaurer, meaning "to restore" (referring to restoring one's strength with food).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "variety" is correctly spelt — it means a number of different types of something.

• Option 3: "dishes" is correctly spelt — the plural of "dish", meaning a particular type of prepared food.

• Option 4: "offers" is correctly spelt — the third-person singular form of the verb "offer".

NOTE

• Other frequently misspelt French-origin words in SSC exams: restaurant, entrepreneur, bureau, connoisseur, questionnaire, liaison.

• A quick trick to remember "restaurant": it contains the word "rant" at the end (rest-au-rant).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
They are building a new hospital in the city.
option_1: A new hospital was built in the city by them.
option_2: A new hospital has been built in the city by them.
option_3: A new hospital will be built in the city by them.
option_4: A new hospital is being built in the city by them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A new hospital is being built in the city by them.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "They are building a new hospital in the city" is in the Present Continuous Tense.

• Rule — Present Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + is/am/are + V1+ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "a new hospital" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary is "is"; "being" is inserted; the verb "build" becomes the past participle "built"; and "they" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: A new hospital is being built by them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was built" is the passive form of the Simple Past Tense, not the Present Continuous Tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "has been built" is the passive form of the Present Perfect Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "will be built" is the passive form of the Simple Future Tense.

NOTE

• Remember the marker word "being" — it is unique to the passive of continuous tenses (Present Continuous and Past Continuous) and must never be dropped.

• Past Continuous passive, for comparison: Active — "They were building a hospital"; Passive — "A hospital was being built by them."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.
As the rulers of the planet, humans like to think that it is the largest creatures that will emerge victorious from the struggle for survival.
option_2: it is the most large creatures
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. they are the largest creatures.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined portion "it is the largest creatures" is grammatically wrong because the singular pronoun "it" and singular verb "is" do not agree with the plural noun "creatures", and both must logically refer back to the plural noun "humans".

• Rule — Pronoun-Antecedent and Subject-Verb Agreement: A pronoun must agree in number with the noun it refers to, and the verb must agree in number with its subject. Since "humans" (plural) is the antecedent, the pronoun must be "they" and the verb must be "are".

• Corrected sentence: "...humans like to think that they are the largest creatures that will emerge victorious from the struggle for survival."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No substitution" is incorrect because the original sentence does contain a clear pronoun-agreement error, as explained above.

• Option 2: "it is the most large creatures" is incorrect because it keeps the wrong singular pronoun "it"/"is", and also wrongly forms the superlative as "most large" instead of "largest".

• Option 3: "they are a largest creature" is incorrect because the article "a" cannot be used with the superlative "largest", and it also wrongly makes "creature" singular after the plural "they are".

NOTE

• Superlative adjectives of one or two syllables (like "large") normally take "-est" (largest), not "most"; "most" is used with longer adjectives (most beautiful, most intelligent).

• The definite article "the" is compulsory before a superlative adjective ("the largest", not just "largest" or "a largest").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Experts acknowledged that some counterfeiting of document techniques are virtually impossible to detect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. forgery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forgery" means the crime of producing a fake document, signature, or work of art in order to deceive (जालसाजी/कूटरचना), which is exactly what "counterfeiting of document" describes.
◦ Example: He was arrested for forgery after submitting fake certificates.

• The underlined phrase "counterfeiting of document" can be replaced by the single word "forgery" without any change in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Fiasco (पूर्ण असफलता): Means a complete failure, especially an embarrassing one — unrelated to faking documents.

• Option 3: Impromptu (बिना तैयारी का): Means done without preparation or planning; unrelated to counterfeiting.

• Option 4: Frenzy (उन्माद): Means a state of wild excitement or uncontrolled behaviour; unrelated to the meaning intended.

NOTE

• Related words: forge (verb, to fake), forger (a person who commits forgery), counterfeit (adjective/verb, fake or to fake, usually used for money or goods).

• Other crime-related one-word substitutes commonly tested: plagiarism (copying another's work), embezzlement (misappropriating funds), fraud (deception for gain).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
They have built a new bridge across the river.
option_1: A new bridge has been built across the river by them.
option_2: A new bridge by them has been built across the river.
option_3: A new bridge has built across the river by them.
option_4: The river has been built a new bridge by them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A new bridge has been built across the river by them.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "They have built a new bridge across the river" is in the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "a new bridge" becomes the subject; since "bridge" is singular, the auxiliary is "has"; "been" is inserted; the verb "build" stays as the past participle "built"; and "they" becomes the agent with "by", placed after the place phrase "across the river".
◦ Passive: A new bridge has been built across the river by them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because the agent phrase "by them" is wrongly placed in the middle of the sentence instead of at the end.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it omits "been", which is compulsory in the passive of the Present Perfect Tense ("has built" is not a valid passive form).

• Option 4 is incorrect because it wrongly makes "the river" the subject, producing the absurd meaning that the river itself has been built.

NOTE

• The word "been" is the tell-tale marker of Present Perfect passive constructions; forgetting it is one of the most common errors in this tense.

• The place phrase (here, "across the river") normally comes before the agent phrase ("by them") in a passive sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank.
The chef requires ______ vegetables for the salad. [stale]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. fresh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stale" means no longer fresh; having lost its original good taste, quality, or crispness (बासी), so its opposite is "fresh", meaning newly made, produced, or picked; not stale (ताज़ा).

• Rule: In such questions, the blank must be filled with a word that is the direct opposite of the word given in brackets, while also making grammatical and contextual sense in the sentence.

• "The chef requires fresh vegetables for the salad" makes complete sense, since a chef would want vegetables that are not stale for preparing a salad.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: green (हरा): Refers to colour, not freshness; not every fresh vegetable is green (e.g., fresh tomatoes are red).

• Option 3: cut (कटा हुआ): Describes vegetables that have been sliced, unrelated to the concept of freshness versus staleness.

• Option 4: leafy (पत्तेदार): Describes a type of vegetable (like spinach), not its freshness.

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs related to food/freshness commonly tested: fresh × rotten, ripe × raw/unripe, crisp × soggy, sweet × sour.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the sentence given below.
I refuse to let anything come in the way of my dreams.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. permit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Refuse" means to indicate or state that one is unwilling to do something or to allow something (मना करना), so its opposite is "permit", meaning to allow or give consent to something (अनुमति देना).

• Rule: Antonym questions require finding the word that directly contradicts the core meaning of the given word — here, denial versus allowance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: repress (दबाना): Means to suppress or restrain a feeling or action; it is close in meaning to refuse/deny, not its opposite.

• Option 2: balk (हिचकना): Means to hesitate or be unwilling to do something; it is a near-synonym of refuse, not an antonym.

• Option 3: accord (प्रदान करना/सामंजस्य): As a verb it can mean to grant, but it is normally used with abstract nouns (accord respect, accord priority) rather than meaning "to allow someone to do something"; "permit" is the more precise and direct antonym of "refuse" here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "refuse": decline, reject, deny, balk, spurn.

• Other antonym pairs of the "allow/deny" type often tested: grant × deny, consent × refuse, approve × reject.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
The principal gave up / the prizes to / the winners on / Republic Day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The principal gave up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the phrasal verb "gave up"; the correct phrasal verb needed here is "gave away", since the principal is distributing/handing out the prizes to the winners, not abandoning or surrendering them.

• Rule — Phrasal verbs: "Give up" means to stop doing something or to surrender/abandon something, whereas "give away" means to distribute or hand over something to someone, especially as a gift or prize.

• Corrected sentence: "The principal gave away the prizes to the winners on Republic Day."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "the winners on" is correct as written; no grammatical error is present in this segment.

• Option 3: "the prizes to" is correct as written; it correctly introduces the indirect object with the preposition "to".

• Option 4: "Republic Day" is correct as written; it is a properly capitalised proper noun used as the time reference.

NOTE

• Commonly confused phrasal verbs with "give": give up (to stop/surrender), give away (to distribute/reveal), give in (to yield/surrender to pressure), give off (to emit, e.g. a smell or gas), give out (to distribute or become exhausted).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words in the following sentence.
Almost immediately, they heard the high shrill piercing cry of tires on the side road.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. screech.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Screech" means a high-pitched, shrill, piercing cry or sound, which is exactly the meaning of the underlined phrase "high shrill piercing cry" — commonly used for the sound of tyres, brakes, or an animal's cry. (तीखी चीख/चरचराहट की आवाज़)
◦ Example: The car came to a stop with a screech of tires.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Beseech (विनती करना): Means to ask someone urgently and earnestly to do something; unrelated to a shrill sound.

• Option 2: Creche (शिशु गृह): Means a nursery where babies and young children are cared for during the working day; unrelated in meaning and sound.

• Option 4: Bleach (विरंजित करना): Means to whiten something using a chemical agent, or the chemical itself; unrelated to sound.

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutes for sounds often tested in SSC: shriek (a sudden sharp cry), wail (a long, mournful cry), whine (a high-pitched complaining sound), squeal (a long high-pitched cry).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Synthetic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Natural.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Synthetic" means made by chemical synthesis, especially to imitate a natural product; artificial (कृत्रिम/संश्लेषित), so its direct opposite is "Natural", meaning existing in or caused by nature; not artificial (प्राकृतिक).

• Rule: Antonym questions require the word that is the exact conceptual opposite; "synthetic" and "natural" form a standard, commonly tested antonym pair.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Artificial (कृत्रिम): Is actually a synonym of synthetic, not its opposite — both describe something man-made rather than natural.

• Option 2: Imitation (नकली): Means something made to look like something else, again close in meaning to synthetic, not opposite to it.

• Option 3: Processed (संसाधित): Means treated or prepared by a particular method; it is related to manufacturing, not the direct opposite of "synthetic".

NOTE

• Other antonym pairs of the "man-made vs. natural" type often tested: Genuine × Fake, Authentic × Counterfeit, Organic × Inorganic/Synthetic.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The adverse (1)_________ of climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly driving human mobility the world over, particularly in countries with high exposure and low (2)_________ capacity. While most climate-related mobility currently occurs within countries, desperation and deteriorating environments can also compel people to seek a livelihood elsewhere through (3)_________ migration. While climate change negatively impacts everyone, everywhere, those already in vulnerable situations due to geography, poverty, gender, age, disability, origin, or other status, including migrant women who (4)_________ climate-sensitive livelihoods, and children who are less able to survive extreme weather events, are at the greatest risk of suffering harm. It is (5)_________ to recognise this reality and take meaningful action to protect the human rights of those most affected by climate change, including migrants.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. effects.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun that can be modified by the adjective "adverse" and can be the subject of the plural verb "are... driving". "Effects" (plural noun, meaning results or consequences) fits perfectly: "adverse effects... are... driving human mobility".

• Rule: "Effect" (noun) means a result or consequence, while "affect" is normally used as a verb meaning to influence. Since the blank needs a noun (it takes the adjective "adverse" before it and the verb "are" after it), "effects" is grammatically required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "renounce" is a verb meaning to formally give up a right, belief, or activity; it cannot function as a noun after "adverse" and does not fit the sentence.

• Option 2: "affects" is grammatically incorrect here because "affect" is primarily a verb, not a noun, and the sentence structure requires a noun subject after "the adverse".

• Option 4: "practice" does not fit the meaning of the sentence, which is about the results/consequences of climate change, not a practice or habit.

NOTE

• Commonly confused pair: effect (noun) = result, e.g. "the effect of the medicine"; affect (verb) = to influence, e.g. "the medicine will affect his health". "Effect" can rarely be used as a verb meaning "to bring about" (e.g. "to effect a change"), and "affect" can rarely be a noun in psychology (meaning emotion/mood) — but for SSC exams, remember the basic rule: effect = noun (result), affect = verb (to influence).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. adaptive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that pairs with "capacity" to describe a country's ability to adjust to the effects of climate change. "Adaptive capacity" is the standard term (commonly used in climate-change literature) for the ability of a system or country to adjust to changing conditions.

• Rule: In cloze passages, always check the word that immediately follows the blank — here "capacity" — since many blanks test fixed collocations (a noun that habitually pairs with a specific adjective).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "adoptive" means related to adoption (as in adoptive parents); it is a commonly confused word with "adaptive" but does not fit the meaning of adjusting to climate change.

• Option 3: "minimum" does not form the required collocation "minimum capacity" in this context and also does not carry the sense of adjusting to change.

• Option 4: "affective" relates to emotions/moods (affective disorders); it is unrelated to the ability to cope with climate change.

NOTE

• Commonly confused word pair: adaptive (relating to adjustment/adapting) vs adoptive (relating to adoption, e.g. adoptive parents/family) — a frequent SSC trap due to similar spelling.

• "Capacity" frequently collocates with words like adaptive, coping, production, and storage in exam passages.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. irregular.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that pairs with "migration" to describe movement undertaken outside formal or legal channels, driven by desperation. "Irregular migration" is the standard term (used in UN/refugee-related literature) for migration that takes place outside the regulatory norms of the countries involved.

• Rule: As with the previous blank, the word immediately following the blank ("migration") signals the required fixed collocation; "irregular migration" is a well-established term in this context, distinct from "regular" or "planned" migration.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "regard" does not collocate meaningfully with "migration" and does not fit the sense of desperate, unplanned movement.

• Option 2: "fast" describes speed, not the legal/formal status of migration, and does not form a recognised collocation with "migration" in this context.

• Option 3: "fixate" is a verb meaning to focus intently on something; it cannot grammatically function as an adjective before "migration".

NOTE

• "Irregular migration" is contrasted with "regular migration" (movement through recognised legal channels) in official and journalistic writing on climate and migration.

• Related terms often seen in such passages: displacement, asylum seekers, climate refugees, forced migration.

It is (5)_________ to recognise this reality and take meaningful action to protect the human rights of those most affected by climate change, including migrants.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. depend on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires the correct preposition to follow the verb "depend". The fixed, standard usage in English is "depend on" (or "depend upon"), meaning to rely on something or be determined by it.

• Rule — Prepositions after verbs: Certain verbs are always followed by a specific preposition; this fixed pairing must be memorised, as no other preposition is grammatically acceptable with "depend" in the standard sense of "to rely on".

• The sentence reads: "...migrant women who depend on climate-sensitive livelihoods...", meaning their livelihoods rely on conditions affected by climate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "depend from" is grammatically incorrect; "from" is not the preposition that follows "depend" in the sense of reliance (it is occasionally used literally to mean "to hang from").

• Option 2: "depend at" is grammatically incorrect; "at" is never used as the preposition following "depend".

• Option 4: "depend in" is grammatically incorrect; "in" is never used as the preposition following "depend".

NOTE

• "Depend on/upon" is one of the most frequently tested fixed prepositional verbs in SSC exams; other examples include: rely on, count on, insist on, congratulate on.

• The related word "dependent" also takes "on": "dependent on someone/something".

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. imperative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word meaning absolutely necessary or urgently required, fitting the phrase "It is _____ to recognise this reality and take meaningful action...". "Imperative" (adjective, meaning extremely important or urgent) fits this sense perfectly.

• Rule: In cloze passages, the correct option must fit both the grammatical structure ("It is + adjective + to + infinitive") and the overall tone/meaning of the passage, which stresses the urgency of protecting vulnerable people from climate change.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "optional" means not compulsory, which directly contradicts the urgent tone the passage is building towards.

• Option 2: "secondary" means of lesser importance, which again contradicts the sense of urgency required by the context.

• Option 3: "resistant" means opposing or not easily affected by something; it does not fit the sense of "necessary to do something" required here.

NOTE

• "Imperative" can be used both as an adjective (urgently necessary) and as a noun (an essential or urgent requirement, e.g. "a moral imperative").

• Synonyms of "imperative" (in this sense) commonly tested: essential, crucial, vital, indispensable, mandatory.
